title: Metro Open Data real-time arrivals API v2 launch

# Release proposal: Metro Open Data — Real-time Arrivals API v2

Owner: Open Data team · Launch: Mon 2026-11-16 · Developer blog post: same day 15:00 local · Change: OD-0412

## Summary

v2 of the public real-time arrivals API adds stop-level crowding, vehicle accessibility features and a single `/v2/arrivals` endpoint that replaces three v1 endpoints. v1 continues to run unchanged until its sunset date.

## Endpoints

| v2 | Replaces (v1) |
|---|---|
| `GET /v2/arrivals?stop_id=…` | `/v1/stops/{id}/predictions`, `/v1/predictions`, `/v1/routes/{id}/stops/{id}` |
| `GET /v2/vehicles?route_id=…` | `/v1/vehicles` |
| `GET /v2/alerts` | `/v1/alerts` (unchanged shape) |

## v2 response changes

- New: `crowding` (`low` / `medium` / `high` / `unknown`), `wheelchair_accessible` (bool), `bike_rack_slots` (int or null), `feed_age_seconds`.
- Removed vs v1: `vehicle_label` (internal fleet label, not useful to riders) and the deprecated `eta_text` string. Clients should format times from `arrival_time` (ISO 8601 with offset).
- No operator/driver identifiers are present in v1 or v2.

## Access and CORS

- Reads are anonymous: no key required up to 60 requests/min per IP.
- Optional free key (header `X-Api-Key`) raises the limit to 1,000 requests/min; keys identify apps for rate limiting and contact, they grant no extra data or write access.
- Responses send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` without `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`; the API sets no cookies and has no authenticated or mutating routes, so browser apps can call it directly.

## v1 deprecation

- v1 keeps its current shape and SLO until sunset on **2027-11-16** (12 months).
- From launch day, v1 responses carry `Deprecation: @1794787200` and `Sunset: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 00:00:00 GMT` headers and a `Link` header to the migration guide.
- Email to all 1,412 registered key holders on launch day, again at 6 months, 3 months and 1 month before sunset. Top 20 consumers by volume (≈ 81% of v1 traffic) get direct outreach from the team.
- Migration guide maps every v1 field to its v2 equivalent, including how to replace `eta_text`.

## Licensing

- Data remains under CC BY 4.0. The blog post, API docs and every response's `meta.license` field carry the attribution text "Contains data from Metro Transit, CC BY 4.0".

## Load and reliability

- Load test on the production-sized staging cluster: 3× current peak (v1 peak 4,100 req/s → 12,300 req/s on v2) for 30 min, p95 38 ms, 0 errors.
- CDN caches `/v2/arrivals` per `stop_id` for 10 s (feed updates every 15 s); `feed_age_seconds` lets apps show staleness.
- If the AVL feed stalls > 90 s, responses keep serving the last good snapshot with `feed_age_seconds` set and `meta.degraded: true`; on-call is paged at 120 s.
- v2 shares the ingestion pipeline with v1 but runs as a separate deployment and autoscaling group, so a v2 fault cannot take down v1.

## QA summary

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Contract tests: 214 cases, v2 schema vs OpenAPI spec | Pass |
| Parity: v2 `arrival_time` vs v1 predictions for 2,000 sampled stop/time pairs | 100% match |
| v1 regression suite against production after v2 deploy to canary | Pass |
| Rate limits: anonymous 61st req/min → 429 with `Retry-After`; keyed limit 1,000 | Pass |
| Degraded mode: AVL feed paused 3 min in staging | Pass, `degraded: true`, page fired at 120 s |
| Developer docs: screen reader check of docs site + code samples have text alternatives | Pass |

## Rollout

1. Deploy v2 service; API gateway routes `/v2/*` only (v1 routes untouched).
2. Canary: 5% of `/v2/*` traffic for 48 h to new instances (traffic only from internal apps and the 3 pilot partners who opted in).
3. Publish docs and blog post; open v2 to all.
4. Advance gates: v2 5xx < 0.1%, p95 < 100 ms, parity monitor ≥ 99.9%.
5. Rollback: gateway route weight for `/v2/*` back to 0 (returns 503 with a link to status page); v1 unaffected. No shared schema changes.

## Blog post (excerpt)

> Today we're launching v2 of the Metro Real-time Arrivals API. New: crowding levels, wheelchair accessibility per vehicle, and bike rack availability. v1 keeps working until Nov 16, 2027. Our migration guide covers every field. Data is CC BY 4.0. Please credit "Metro Transit" in your app.
decoys: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * looks like a CORS hole, but the API is anonymous, read-only, sets no cookies, has no authenticated or mutating routes, and does not send Allow-Credentials. Keys only raise rate limits.

v2 removes vehicle_label and eta_text, which looks like a breaking change for clients. v1 is unchanged until a 12-month sunset with Deprecation/Sunset headers, staged emails and direct outreach, and the migration guide maps every field.
